transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Rachel Park (Meridian Head of ML), Samir Patel (Meridian CTO), Lena Ortiz (Meridian SRE)

Summary:
Redwood team (AE+SE) and Meridian Health scoped a 6-week POC to validate model serving performance and cost for a clinical summarization workload. Discussed success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark metrics, timeline milestones (kickoff, infra access, mid-point review, exec readout), and security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS). Agreed next steps and owners.

Key topics:
- POC objectives and success criteria (latency, throughput, quality thresholds)
- Workload sizing: token rates, concurrency, dataset size
- Benchmarks: latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, throughput on Dedicated vs Hosted
- Timeline & milestones: kickoff, access/setup, midpoint demo, exec readout
- Security: SOC2, VPC/VPN, KMS, audit logs

Action items (recap at end): see action_items metadata above.

Transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining today, appreciate you blocking time. quick roll call?
00:06 Rachel Park: hi this is rachel, i'm head of ml at meridian, hey!
00:09 Samir Patel: samir here, cto, good to meet you both
00:12 Lena Ortiz: hi lena, s r e, i'll handle infra stuff
00:15 Maya Chen: awesome, i'm maya from redwood and daniel our se is on the call. daniel you want to intro real quick?
00:20 Daniel Ortiz: yep, daniel ortiz, infra and performance at redwood. i run benchmarks and set up dedicated clusters for poc.
00:26 Maya Chen: cool. goal for today is to align on POC scope — success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and a proposed timeline with milestones. we have about an hour. sound good?
00:36 Rachel Park: perfect, yes. quick context: we want to embed a clinical note summarization feature into our provider portal. must be fast (<500ms p50 ideally), and cost needs to be reasonable because we're doing a lot of records per day. data is PHI so we need private deployment or strict vpc and kms controls.
00:53 Maya Chen: got it. thanks rachel. daniel, can you walk through typical success criteria you see?
00:58 Daniel Ortiz: sure. typically we split success into three buckets: latency & throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics (rouge/bleu-ish and human evals). for latency we aim for p50 and p95 targets, e.g. p50 <500ms for short requests, p95 <1200ms depending on batch sizes. throughput: target sustained concurrency of about 50 concurrent requests for the POC environment and burst to 100. cost: measure end-to-end cost per 1k tokens for inference and bandwidth. quality we validate against your test set and some manual spot checks. also rollout criteria — if dedicated meets cost+latency and passes quality, recommend dedicated for production.
01:45 Rachel Park: that aligns. quick note on transcripts: our average input is 400 tokens and outputs 120 tokens, but worst-case can be 1,200 tokens with longer consult notes. typical daily volume for pilot is ~150k input tokens/day, but we might scale up to 1.5M if we go into production.
02:05 Daniel Ortiz: good to know. for sizing that means we should benchmark with a mix: 80% at 400-in/120-out, 15% at 1,200-in, and 5% long tail. we'll include KV cache warmup patterns — sorry i said K-V cash earlier — key value cache behavior matters for summaries when clients do multi-turn?
02:26 Lena Ortiz: quick question, do you support private deployments in our VPC and integrate with our KMS?
02:30 Maya Chen: yes, redwood private supports customer VPC and HSM/KMS integrations; we also have options for a private control plane. daniel can speak to what we need from infra.
02:38 Daniel Ortiz: infrastructure-wise we need a peered VPC or VPN, a bastion for deploy access and a small service account that can access test buckets. for KMS we support customer-managed keys; we'll need an IAM role and the key ARN. firewall rules: allow outbound to our control plane on port 443 (or alternately we can run fully air-gapped for on-prem).
03:01 Samir Patel: on air-gap, we prefer not to be fully air-gapped initially. VPC peering with strict egress rules sounds right.
03:07 Rachel Park: security questions: do you have SOC2 and audit logs? and how long do you retain logs?
03:13 Maya Chen: yes SOC2, and we can provide the report. audit log retention is configurable; standard is 90 days but enterprise retention is available. we'll attach the security whitepaper.
03:24 Daniel Ortiz: for the POC, we'll enable detailed tracing and token-level cost metrics so you can see p99 latencies and token counts per request.
03:31 Samir Patel: great. timeline — what are you proposing?
03:34 Maya Chen: we propose a 6-week POC:
03:37 Maya Chen: Week 0: Kickoff + access setup (week of Aug 17)
03:42 Maya Chen: Week 1-2: baseline benchmarks (hosted and dedicated profiles), initial quality evals
03:46 Maya Chen: Week 3: mid-point review + performance tuning
03:49 Maya Chen: Week 4-5: run extended benchmarks, cost modeling, and security validation
03:53 Maya Chen: Week 6: exec readout and recommendation for next steps (production path)
04:00 Rachel Park: that seems reasonable. we have an exec readout window in first week of September, so week 6 lining up makes sense.
04:08 Daniel Ortiz: concrete kickoff actions: we'll need test dataset upload instructions, list of sample prompts, max concurrency pattern, and credentials for VPN/VPC peering. we'll draft a benchmark plan with the scenarios I mentioned.
04:23 Lena Ortiz: for VPN we'll share a ticket with our infra team and the egress policy; expect to provide a pre-provisioned peering and a test service account.
04:30 Maya Chen: perfect. success criteria — rachel, can you outline the must-have thresholds?
04:36 Rachel Park: must-haves: p50 < 500ms for typical 400 token input, p95 < 1500ms; quality: automated metrics above baseline and no critical hallucinations in spot checks; security: SOC2 and KMS integration confirmed. stretch: cost under $X per 1k tokens — i'll confirm the exact number and add to the doc.
04:58 Daniel Ortiz: ok we'll capture that as the POC gating criteria. for benchmarks we'll compare hosted vs dedicated across quantized and fp16 profiles, and report latency/cost tradeoffs.
05:12 Samir Patel: are you able to run benchmarks with our mixed-concurrency shapes? e.g. evenings have 3x traffic spikes.
05:18 Daniel Ortiz: yes, we'll simulate diurnal patterns and burst spikes. we'll also test prefix caching behavior for repeated patient lookups to measure KV/cache hit improvements.
05:29 Rachel Park: small clarification: will Redwood run the benchmarks inside our VPC, or do you prefer to run them from your control plane?
05:36 Daniel Ortiz: ideally we run within your VPC for private deployment tests; for hosted runs we can run from our cluster. we'll give you scripts to run inside your environment as well.
05:46 Lena Ortiz: what about data anonymization? we can provide de-identified samples but security will want to see the end-to-end using synthetic PHI for some tests.
05:55 Maya Chen: that's fine; synthetic/de-identified data for the bulk plus a small real sample under NDA for quality checks if you want.
06:02 Rachel Park: yes we'll prepare a de-id set and a 100-case real sample under NDA.
06:07 Daniel Ortiz: perfect. benchmarks we'll measure: p50/p95/p99, tail latencies, throughput (reqs/sec), token/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and quality diffs vs current baseline. we'll produce a spreadsheet with per-scenario numbers.
06:25 Samir Patel: for cost calc do you include network egress and tokenization overhead?
06:30 Daniel Ortiz: yes, we include inference GPU time, orchestration overhead, and network egress where applicable. we'll show both raw inference cost and end-to-end billable cost.
06:41 Maya Chen: ok let's talk deliverables and owners. daniel will own the benchmark plan. maya will own pricing/SOW/security docs. lena will own infra access. rachel will own success criteria and dataset. samir will finalize exec readout invite list.
06:55 Rachel Park: sounds good. can we also have a mid-point demo script — what do you typically show?
07:01 Daniel Ortiz: at the midpoint we demo baseline results vs targets, show tuning we did (batch sizes, quantization, model variants), and provide a recommended running config for production. it's usually a 30 minute demo + 15 minute q&a.
07:16 Samir Patel: and for the exec readout we want a 15 minute summary: cost savings, latency improvements, recommended path (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
07:24 Maya Chen: noted. any legal/procurement constraints we should be aware of?
07:29 Samir Patel: standard enterprise contract with data processing addendum and indemnity language. procurement can turn quickly but we'll try to get SOW signed after POC if results look good.
07:39 Rachel Park: one more technical clar: do you support custom tokenizers or tokenization differences across models? sometimes our clinical abbreviations tokenization matters.
07:47 Daniel Ortiz: we support passing pre-tokenized inputs and custom tokenizer configs for private deployments. we'll verify tokenization parity during the quality checks.
07:56 Maya Chen: ok to recap:
07:58 Maya Chen: - Redwood to send SOW/pricing and SOC2, security pack by Aug 13
08:04 Maya Chen: - Meridian to provide de-identified dataset and 100-case sample by Aug 14
08:08 Maya Chen: - infra team (Lena) to share VPN/VPC peering details by Aug 14
08:12 Maya Chen: - Redwood (Daniel) to deliver benchmark plan by Aug 18
08:17 Maya Chen: - Kickoff proposed week of Aug 17 with infra support
08:22 Rachel Park: confirmed on those dates, i'll add specifics on cost target in the doc and post it to the shared drive.
08:29 Samir Patel: we'll block exec readout slot first week of Sept, tentatively Sept 2.
08:34 Maya Chen: great we'll send calendar invites after kickoff confirmation.
08:38 Maya Chen: any final questions?
08:40 Lena Ortiz: one more on observability — does Redwood provide token-level tracing in production?
08:44 Daniel Ortiz: yes we provide token-level cost breakdowns and latency per token, plus per-route dashboards in the console. logs can be routed to your SIEM or exported via S3.
08:56 Rachel Park: perfect. i'm comfortable with next steps. thanks everyone.
08:59 Maya Chen: thank you all, we'll follow up with the documents. talk soon.
09:03 [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words, filler words and shorthand inferred; speaker labels are from calendar join and may not exactly match tone.
